remove: The one-item 'BRANDY' H3 label. It heads a single row, breaks the De agave / Brandy rhythm, and adds a third tier inside a four-row column. Fold Cognac VSOP under a plain 'Destilados' list, or relabel the column once.
top_problem: The lower two-column grid does not balance. The Sidra column holds one item over a 37.5 mm hole, and the paired columns end 24.7 mm and 14.6 mm apart. The full-width cocktail band leaves 40-75 mm of empty right side on every name row. The grid is exact at the left edges but not filled. The boldest missing idea is a structural one: the contour-ploughed rows in the art should drive the text grid, with ruled rows or bands that carry the Iowa fields into the reading area. At the moment the reading area is a generic editorial list beside a painting.
fixes: Rebalance the paired grid so columns end within one 7 pt row. For example, put all of Beer & Cider (3 drafts + Sidra/cider) in the left column and Destilados in the right on the same 282-420 | 438-576 pt band, then set Vino beside them or full width. This removes the 48.7 x 37.5 mm hole under Dry Cider and the 14.6 mm Wine/Spirits mismatch.
Set Cocktails on the same two-column grid (Clásicos | De la casa, 282-420 | 438-576 pt) so all three sections use one grid. The 42-77 mm empty right band on the cocktail name rows then has a job.

Lock rows in paired columns to shared baselines. Give the spirit rows the wine rows' 35 pt pitch, or align row tops, so Añejo (216.19 mm) sits level with Pinot Grigio (221.13) and Cognac with Espumosos/Brut Rosé.
Put the allergen line on the 35 pt section gap (it is 40.36 pt now), or anchor it to the bottom margin with a deliberate rule, so the last section gap matches 12.8 mm.

Centre CANTINA in its lane: 2.7 mm to the torn edge against 8.1 mm to the reading column. Drop the sensory italic from 11 pt to 10.5 pt (or ingredients to 10 pt) so the item stack steps down in size, not up.

lens: typography and hierarchy (display wordmark, bilingual heads)

measurements.item_gaps_pt: 7 within single-row subs, 14 between cocktail blocks; measured on the page, the H3 'DE LA CASA' sits about 0.65x as far below the Manhattan block as Manhattan sits below the Margarita block, so the subhead groups with the section above it
measurements.h3_weight_mismatch: in the render the Spanish half of each H3 looks like DM Sans italic around 400 and the English half like 700 (spec says 700 for both)
measurements.dead_space: Sidra column is empty below Dry Cider for about 150 pt; the Spirits column ends about 65 pt above Wine; the gap from the Daiquiri to the Beer H2 is visibly larger than the other section gaps; the bottom right third is empty above the allergen line
measurements.wordmark: CANTINA in Fraunces opsz 144 at weight 380, 96 pt vertical, ink top 36.0 pt matches the first H2 cap line

top_problem: The type system has too many voices and a broken proximity logic. Four text treatments sit under each name (italic sensory line, 10.5 pt roman ingredients, 9 pt tracked Fraunces caps, green price), plus a two-family H2 and a two-weight DM Sans H3. The garnish-and-glass caps line is nearly as heavy as the item name, the H3 Spanish/English halves render at visibly different weights, and 'DE LA CASA' sits closer to the Manhattan than to its own item. The wordmark is an elegant fashion Didone in the Bistro reference's lane rather than an ownable cantina voice. The boldest missing idea is a bilingual typographic system as the concept itself: Spanish and English set as one deliberately paired voice, with the wordmark drawn from that same pairing, instead of a borrowed vertical wordmark beside a tidy list.
remove: the Fraunces 9 pt tracked-caps garnish · glass treatment (a third caps voice that competes with the names); set it in the sensory italic at the muted colour instead
fixes: Set the garnish · glass line in Newsreader italic 10 pt #5A4B3F in lowercase (or drop the caps to weight 400 with .04em tracking) so each cocktail has a clear 1-2-3 descent: name, then the sensory and ingredient lines, then the serve line.

Give the H3 halves one weight (both DM Sans 700, or Spanish 500 italic against English 500 roman) so each bilingual label reads as one unit, and give BRANDY a matching pair or drop the H3 and let Cognac sit under De agave with a 14 pt gap.
Fix proximity: put 21 pt above every H3 that follows an item block and keep 7 pt below it, so 'DE LA CASA' (and 'ESPUMOSOS', 'BRANDY') clearly belong to the items that follow them.

Close the dead fields: move Dry Cider under the draft beers (keep 'Sidra · Cider' as its H3) or bring Spirits up beside Beer, so the two-column blocks end within 14 pt of each other and the Daiquiri-to-Beer gap matches the other section gaps.

Give the wordmark a venue-specific voice (a heavier, warmer display cut, or the bilingual lock-up 'CANTINA · & cocktail bar' set on the same Newsreader/Fraunces pairing as the H2s) so it stops reading as a close copy of ref-01's Didone 'BISTRO'.

top_problem: All the palette's colour and all the concept live in the left rail. The reading column is dark ink on cream with a price green too close in value to the black names to register, so the numbers neither stand out nor tie to the art. The boldest missing idea: let the agave and loess colours structure the menu itself, for example section H2s keyed to the rail's contour bands, so the art and the list read as one collage rather than a picture beside a list.
remove: The Spirits sub-labels 'DE AGAVE · AGAVE' and 'BRANDY'. Three name-only rows under a bilingual H2 do not need two more rust labels, and the rust labels become 8 equal accent hits competing across the column.
fixes: Separate the prices from the names by value, not only hue. Move the price ink to a mid agave green such as #2E5A4B (about 6.5:1 on #F2E9D6, above 4.5:1 at the worst pixel) or keep #27463A and drop the weight to 500 against the 600 names, so the numbers register as a distinct quiet voice without shouting.

Fix the empty pocket under Sidra (about 40 x 25 mm) and the uneven column ends. Stack Cider under Draft, or rebalance Wine and Spirits, so the paired columns end within one 7 pt line of each other and every empty area has a job.

Carry one rail colour into the reading structure. Recolour the four H2 rules from #6B5A4C to the loess terracotta #B5532F or the dark agave green #27463A, so the column visibly belongs to the collage (the gold stays sun-only, per the thesis).

Strengthen the rust H3 labels for bar light. The Spanish italic half measures 5.19:1 at the worst pixel at 9 pt light-weight caps; darken to the loess dark #7C3322 (about 8:1) or set both halves at 700 weight.

Tighten the 35 pt section gap after House Daiquiri and remove the floating gap above the allergen line. Pin the allergen line to the column's last baseline rhythm so the page ends on the grid rather than in open cream.

top_problem: The art is fenced off in a left strip, so the torn-paper idea never reaches the words. The sun, agave and contour rows sit beside the menu, not in it. The CANTINA wordmark doesn't touch the sun (Solstice runs its wordmark straight through its sun disk). The contour-ploughed Iowa fields, the one ownable idea here, read as generic brown and green stripes and never come back as structure on the text side. Pass the image-substitution test and it swaps for any Southwest agave-sunset poster. The single boldest missing idea: make the torn contour rows the menu's own architecture, with each section sitting on its own torn furrow band and the sun rising behind the wordmark, so Iowa soil and Mexican agave hold the drinks instead of framing them.
remove: The H2 hairline rules under each section head. They duplicate the job of the terracotta H3 labels and the bilingual H2 scale, and they are the only non-paper device on a page whose thesis is torn paper. Replace them with a torn-edge furrow or with nothing.
fixes: Carry the collage into the type: use a torn contour-row strip (same fibre rim and grain) as the section divider or base for each H2, and cut the vertical CANTINA from, or overlap it onto, the sun disk so word and image lock together (word_image_integration_pass).

Make the Iowa half readable without the proposal: give the contour rows real field geometry (curving terraced furrows with perspective, one strip in corn-gold stubble, loess bluff silhouettes that match Iowa's Loess Hills rather than generic desert peaks), so the art fails the substitution test for any other venue.

Give the empty pockets a job: move Dry Cider under the draft beers and bring Spirits up beside Beer, or put one small torn-paper agave-leaf or furrow vignette in the Sidra/Spirits hole, so the two lower columns end within 7 pt of each other (fix_dead_space).

Close the 18 mm dead band between the vertical wordmark and the text column: either let the torn edge carry the wordmark, set on the paper tear, or tighten the text column left so CANTINA reads as the spine of the page.

Add one quiet materiality move tied to the thesis on the text side, such as a faint deckle or fibre edge on the right trim or a single print-registration offset in the agave green on the prices, so the right 70 % reads as the same hand-cut sheet and not a clean digital page beside a collage.

lens: phone (preview-phone.png) and how print and phone hold together

measurements.price_system: inline, 1 em after the name, one style on print and phone; the right-edge spread (98.1 / 45.8 / 32.3 pt) does not apply to inline prices
measurements.header_sizes: H2 16.5 pt, H3 9 pt, one style per level; H2 x 282/282/438

measurements.phone: 1170 x 7176 px, 24 px sides, 61 row tops on the 8 px grid, minimum type 12 px; each H2 stacks onto 2 lines at display size

top_problem: The phone drops the print's one big idea (a vertical CANTINA rising from a torn page with the sun behind it). What remains is a generic centred hero, a thin horizontal wordmark, and then about 2000 CSS px of an evenly weighted list with no art-to-type link. The two versions share a palette, not a concept. The boldest missing idea is to carry the torn-page edge and the contour-row strata into the reading column as the section dividers, on both formats, so the Iowa field literally structures the menu.
remove: The H2 hairline rules on phone. The stacked Spanish-over-English H2 already separates the sections, and each rule adds a third band per header. Also consider dropping the H2 rule under the half-width Wine/Spirits heads in print.
fixes: Phone: set the H2 on one line ('Cócteles · Cocktails') at about 22 px instead of stacking two display lines, so each section head stops eating about 90 px and the list gains the rhythm of the print version.

Phone: carry the vertical-wordmark idea across. Let CANTINA overlap the hero's torn edge, or set it large across the sun, instead of a thin centred word under the art. Justify the tagline normally, not with the wide gap around the '·'.

Both: use torn contour-strip fragments from the art as the section breaks between Cocktails / Beer / Wine / Spirits. This ties image to word (it passes the substitution test) and replaces the plain rules.
Print: fill or close the dead field under Dry Cider and the short Spirits column. Balance the column ends to within 14 pt, or move the allergen line up to close the gap of about 60 pt.

Both: open the space above each H3 to at least the 14 pt block gap (the 'De la casa' head currently hugs the Manhattan serve line), and give House cocktails one grouping cue (weight or a subtle enclosure) so the reading path has a second focal point after the masthead.

top_problem: Nothing is missing, invented or wrong: all 14 draft items print, all 14 prices match exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, House Daiquiri 14, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18), and there are no item-fact taglines. But half the menu cannot meet criterion 8. Beer has no style or ABV, wine has no grape-region pairing, spirits have no type or age, and the sensory trims leave some lines very thin: 'Toasty'; 'Hop-forward, draft', which repeats the DRAFT label; and 'Dry, sparkling' printed word for word under both Dry Cider and Brut Rosé.
problems: Criterion 8: 7 of 14 items (3 beers, 2 still wines, Brut Rosé, Dry Cider) have no style/ABV or grape/region, and 3 spirits have no type or age. All are properly flagged in meta.missing and needs_input 2-6, so none of it is invented, but the printed menu is still thin.
Two items in different sections print the same sensory line, 'Dry, sparkling' (Dry Cider and Brut Rosé), so neither line tells the reader anything about its own item.
The IPA line was reworded from 'Hop-forward draft IPA' to 'Hop-forward, draft'. The added comma turns 'draft' into a tasting word, and it repeats the DE BARRIL · DRAFT label right above it.
'Toasty' is one word under Amber Lager and reads unfinished next to the fuller cocktail blocks.

The Manhattan prints 'rye whiskey · sweet vermouth' with the bitters hidden, while the Old Fashioned prints aromatic bitters. A guest reads this as the Manhattan having no bitters. It is flagged (needs_input 11) but it reads unevenly.
The House Daiquiri ingredient order (syrup before lime) rests on a Coordinator override of the DB role 'House prep' (needs_input 13). It is presentation only, but it is still open.

Only the Margarita has a sensory line among the cocktails, so the cocktail stack is uneven. This is correct under Rob's rule, but the house cocktails, which should lead a cantina, read barer than the classics.

Reading path: the entry is clear (CANTINA wordmark, then Cocktails). The order cocktails, beer & cider, wine, spirits is sound, and moving cider under Beer is a reasonable regrouping from the draft's last position. But the empty field below Dry Cider and the uneven column endings (Wine ends lower than Spirits) weaken the flow of the lower grid. Agave spirits, the category a cantina should lead with, sit last in a narrow half column.

Price format is one inline system: a bare integer 1 em after the name, tabular, agave green, with eye travel no more than 0.08 of the column. It is consistent but plain. The Brut Rosé price has no glass/bottle label (needs_input 5).
fixes: Get the missing beer style/ABV, wine region and spirit type/age filled in (needs_input 2-6) and print them in the existing one-line format, e.g. 'Pilsner · 4.8%', 'Mendoza'.

Separate the two identical 'Dry, sparkling' lines by printing the draft sentences with only the period dropped: 'Dry sparkling cider' and 'Dry sparkling rosé'. This repeats the class word but keeps each line tied to its own item.
Print the IPA line as the draft has it, 'Hop-forward draft IPA', without the period, or drop 'draft' as already said by its label. Do not insert a comma the draft does not have.
Get needs_input 11 answered (Manhattan bitters) and needs_input 13 answered (Daiquiri syrup role) before approval, so the cocktail ingredient lines rest on source data, not overrides.

Label the Brut Rosé price as glass or bottle once needs_input 5 is answered, and fill the empty space under Dry Cider with the Mexican lager or mezcal lines from needs_input 7 if the venue supplies them. Never add them as placeholders.

lens: ingredient names and description completeness (public_components aware)
top_problem: Every price and item is correct, but the descriptions below the cocktails are thin. The cocktail rows are complete and correctly sourced. The Manhattan's aromatic bitters are rightly hidden because public_components has aromatic-bitters:false. After the cocktails, though, the descriptions shrink to trimmed fragments: Amber Lager prints only 'Toasty'; IPA prints 'Hop-forward, draft', which repeats its own 'De barril · Draft' heading; Brut Rosé prints 'Dry, sparkling', which repeats the 'Espumosos · Sparkling' heading; and Dry Cider is identical, 'Dry, sparkling'. The beer rows have no ABV and the wine rows have no region. These gaps are honestly flagged (needs_input 2-4), not invented, but beer and wine read half-finished next to the four-line cocktail blocks. Checked against /home/user/phg-harmony-app/handoff/designs/test-1-iowa-city-cantina/build/draft_doc.json: all 14 items and all 14 prices match (15/15/16/14, 7/8/7, 8, 12/11/13, 12/16/18). Nothing is invented, and Junmai Ginjo is correctly omitted as retired. Ingredient names trace to the components: 'fresh lime' is a trim of 'Fresh Lime Juice', and 'house demerara syrup' is backed by the House prep role and the draft Daiquiri desc. The Daiquiri's syrup-before-lime order rests on a Coordinator override that is flagged as needs_input 13. The only side-rail text is '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA', which is generic, so it passes. Other issues: (a) the Old Fashioned prints full ingredients while its meta.public_visibility.house_recipe is false; this is not a gate fail because ingredients:true, but it is unconfirmed. (b) The Old Fashioned breaks after 'brown butter-washed bourbon ·', leaving one ingredient alone on line 1, which breaks the proposal's own rule against a lone ingredient on a line. (c) Brown butter (dairy) is shown with only the generic allergen line. (d) Reading path: the 96 pt CANTINA wordmark competes with the Cocktails H2 as the entry point, and the Sidra column and the space under Spirits leave holes, so the lower grid is uneven.
fixes: Replace the three heading-repeating trims: print 'Hop-forward' for the IPA, and 'Dry' or the verbatim 'Dry sparkling rosé' / 'Dry sparkling cider' for the Rosé and Cider, so no descriptor repeats the H3 above it (IPA 'draft', Rosé 'sparkling'). For Amber Lager, print the verbatim 'Toasty amber lager' instead of the one-word 'Toasty'.

Get needs_input 2 and 4 answered (beer ABV and brewery, wine region) and print them as one quiet spec line per row (for example '4.8% · Iowa City, IA' or 'Mendoza, Argentina'); until then beer and wine fall short of the scorecard's style + ABV and grape + region standard.
Re-break the Old Fashioned as 'brown butter-washed bourbon · house demerara syrup ·' / 'aromatic bitters', or widen the measure so it sets on one line, so line 1 is not a lone ingredient.

Before printing, confirm with Rob that meta.public_visibility.house_recipe=false on the Old Fashioned still allows the ingredient list, and get the dairy allergen wording (needs_input 1) so brown butter carries a specific note, not just the generic line.

Fill the empty space below Sidra and below Cognac VSOP, for example by moving Cider under the draft beers or balancing the Wine and Spirits columns, and cut the CANTINA wordmark's pull (lower contrast or weight) so the Cocktails H2 is the single entry point.

lens: flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The reading path is clear through Cocktails, then breaks up in the lower half. The Beer & Cider row is lopsided: Draft has three items and Sidra has one, which leaves an empty pocket under Dry Cider. Spirits stops about 120 pt above Wine, and there is an unexplained gap under the Daiquiri. So after the Cocktails block the eye reads empty space as the end of the menu, instead of reading grouping. The page is correct and follows one grammar, but it reads as a safe template rather than a flow built for a cantina, where the agave program should be a real destination and not a 3-row tail.
problems: Prices: all 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Old Fashioned 16, Daiquiri 14, Pilsner 7, IPA 8, Amber 7, Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco 12, Añejo 16, Cognac VSOP 18). The retired Junmai Ginjo is correctly left out. Nothing is invented.

Cider moved from its own last section in the draft into 'Cerveza y sidra'. The proposal gives the reason (its format is unknown, so it gets its own label). This is acceptable, but 'sidra' now appears in both the H2 and the H3, which is redundant.
Side rail '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' and the allergy line are generic, with no item facts. They pass.

Inline prices sit 1 em after each name, so price right edges spread 98 pt in cocktails and 46/32 pt in the paired columns. The format is consistent (no $, whole numbers, tabular green figures) and every price stays attached to its item. It is not a strong row grid, though.

Criterion 5: there is one clear entry point (CANTINA plus Cócteles) and the top-to-bottom order is logical (cocktails > beer & cider > wine > spirits). But in the lower two-column band the eye can read across (Draft to Cider, Wine to Spirits) or down, and neither path is signalled. Column ends are uneven (Cider ends at about y 1100 of 2000 against Amber Lager at about 1270; Spirits at about 1650 against Brut Rosé at about 1760).

In the Cocktails block, the 'DE LA CASA' label sits closer to the Manhattan serve line above it than the Margarita-to-Manhattan gap does. This weakens the Clásicos / De la casa grouping, which is the main grouping cue in the section.
The gap between the Daiquiri serve line and the Beer H2 looks larger than the other section breaks, so it reads as a hard stop.

For a Mexican bar, the agave spirits (Blanco and Añejo Tequila) come last and are the lightest block on the page: name and price only, in a half column. That is correct by Rob's stack, but the flow does not use them as a destination. Emphasis here should come from grouping, not placement claims.

Criterion 8: the Manhattan prints only one ingredient after its base spirit (bitters hidden per public_components). This is correctly flagged as needs_input 11, but it fails the check that a cocktail names its spirit plus 2 further ingredients. The wines print no grape region and the beers no ABV. Both are flagged in meta.missing, not invented, so this is acceptable but thin. 'Toasty' alone is a weak sensory line for Amber Lager, though it is verbatim from the source.
The Daiquiri places demerara before lime by Coordinator override against the database role 'House prep'. It is flagged as needs_input 13 and does not break the gate, but it is still open.
fixes: Balance the lower grid so columns end together: put Draft and Cider in one column (under a single 'Cerveza y sidra' head, without the duplicate 'Sidra · Cider' H3 if a quiet format note can do its job), or pair Beer & Cider with Spirits and Wine with nothing. Every column in the band should end within one 14 pt line of its neighbour.
Put at least 14 pt above each H3 sub-label and hold the 7 pt gap below it, so 'DE LA CASA · HOUSE' groups visibly with the Old Fashioned and not the Manhattan.
Make the gap after the Daiquiri equal to the other section breaks (35 pt + H2 block), so the Cocktails-to-Beer transition reads as a section break and not the end of the menu.

For the venue, consider ordering the lower band Destilados (agave) beside or before Vino, so the tequila list sits in the reading path. Use grouping or enclosure only; make no placement-for-sales claims.
Get the open inputs (Manhattan bitters display, wine region/grape, beer ABV, Daiquiri demerara role), so every description meets the per-category standard without inventing anything.

lens: voice and consistency across descriptions, bilingual headings and venue copy, venue-type fit (Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: The descriptions don't share one voice. Mechanically trimming the class nouns leaves stubs: the Amber Lager reads 'Toasty' and the IPA reads 'Hop-forward, draft', where 'draft' just repeats the DE BARRIL · DRAFT label. The Czech Pilsner, Malbec and Pinot Grigio keep their class nouns ('Crisp pale lager', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine'), and the cider and the rosé print the same 'Dry, sparkling'. So each beer and wine row reads like a database class, not a line a guest would enjoy, and the bilingual system is applied unevenly. Checked against build/draft_doc.json: all 14 prices match exactly, no items were invented, Junmai Ginjo is correctly left out as retired, there are no taglines, and the side rail ('& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA') is generic venue copy with no item facts. Three voice slips remain. 'Cerveza y sidra · Beer & Cider' is followed by the subhead 'Sidra · Cider', so cider is labelled twice. 'BRANDY' is the only English-only H3 and drops the italic-Spanish · roman-English pattern. The ingredients say 'tequila blanco' while the spirits list says 'Blanco Tequila', two word orders for the same spirit. For a cantina, agave is the least prominent category (half a column at the bottom right, below wine). The Manhattan prints only 2 ingredients (bitters hidden), under the scorecard's spirit-plus-two check, though this is flagged as needs_input 11. Beer ABV/style and wine region are missing but properly flagged, not invented. That is why criterion 8 is held down, not failed.
fixes: Apply one sensory-line rule to every beer, wine and cider row: either print the menu_description verbatim minus only the period (so 'Toasty amber lager', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Dry sparkling rosé'), or print none at all. Don't leave one-word stubs like 'Toasty', or 'draft' repeating its own section label.

Remove the duplicate cider label: either drop the H3 'Sidra · Cider' and keep Dry Cider as a clearly separate right-column group, or rename the H2 'Cerveza · Beer' and keep 'Sidra · Cider' as a sibling H3, so cider is named once.

Make the Brandy H3 follow the same bilingual pattern as the other H3s, with an italic Spanish half and a roman English half (or leave it as one word but in the same italic-plus-roman treatment), so every H3 follows one rule.

Settle on one word order for tequila across the menu ('tequila blanco' / 'tequila añejo' or 'Blanco Tequila' / 'Añejo Tequila') by asking the Coordinator to confirm the display name, not by editing the source names.

For a cantina, give the agave spirits more weight through grouping and hierarchy. For example, place 'Destilados · Spirits' before wine in the reading path, or give 'De agave' its own column head. Keep the mezcal and other gap questions (needs_input 7) open, not filled in.

lens: missing data: how gaps are flagged, and whether anything was invented to fill them
top_problem: The gaps are flagged well on paper, but the guest never sees any sign of them, and the design hides that. All 14 prices match the draft (Junmai Ginjo is retired, so leaving it out is correct), and nothing was made up to fill a gap. But criterion 8 needs beer style + ABV, wine grape + region, and spirit type/age. What prints is a bare 'Toasty', 'Dry red wine' and name-only spirits. Brut Rosé 13 sits in the same column as the 12 and 11 glass pours with no glass or bottle label. The guest will read it as a glass price, and if it is actually a bottle, the menu misstates the price even though the number is correct. The missing_ingredients table is complete: beer, cider, wine, rosé, spirits, Manhattan bitters, Old Fashioned dairy and the new Daiquiri row. It matches doc.json item.meta.missing item by item. The allergy line ('Please tell your server about any allergies.') is generic, makes no claim about any item, and is correctly kept apart from needs_input 1 (the dairy wording). needs_input 13 states the override honestly. The Daiquiri's print order (syrup before lime) still rests on a Coordinator guess that the 'House prep' row is a sweetener, not on the database. It is disclosed, but it is not yet sourced. The 'CANTINA / & Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa' lock-up stands in for the venue name. The draft title is 'Bar menu' and needs_input 8 is still open. The wordmark reads as a real name, although it is generic wording from the brief.
fixes: Resolve needs_input 5 before print: once the Brut Rosé format is known, add a 'copa' or 'botella' pour label on its row (or under the Espumosos label). Until then, show a visible proof-stage placeholder rather than a bare 13 next to the glass pours.

Put the missing guest facts at the top of the Coordinator's ask. Beer ABV and style (needs_input 2), wine region (needs_input 4) and spirit age statement (needs_input 6) are what hold criterion 8 in the 60s; the design cannot fix this.

Get Rob to confirm needs_input 13 and correct the Daiquiri's demerara syrup role in recipe_versions 14d45e57 before publication. If he does not, drop ROLE_OVERRIDE and print in database order (white rum · fresh lime · house demerara syrup), so print order never depends on an unsourced role.

Mark 'CANTINA' and '& Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa' in doc.json meta.missing as a placeholder until needs_input 8 gives the venue name, so a generic descriptor is not published as if it were the brand.

Change the IPA sensory line 'Hop-forward, draft' to 'Hop-forward'. 'Draft' repeats the 'De barril · Draft' label directly above it, and the trimmed fragment reads like a gap-filler rather than a description.

lens: I traced every printed ingredient, garnish, glass label, sensory line and heading on the round-21 letter preview back to build/draft_doc.json and to phg.menu_items joined to phg.recipe_versions (gateway log_id 283). 14 of 14 approved items are printed. Junmai Ginjo is status='retired', so leaving it out is correct.
verified: Margarita: printed 'LIME WHEEL · ROCKS' matches recipe_versions f06abb74 (garnish 'Lime wheel', glassware 'Rocks'). The ingredients tequila blanco, orange liqueur, agave syrup and fresh lime match draft components Tequila Blanco, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup and Fresh Lime Juice. 'Bright and citrus-forward' is verbatim from menu_items.menu_description.

Manhattan: 'COCKTAIL CHERRY · COUPE' matches rv 9fb77eaa (garnish 'Cocktail cherry', glassware 'Coupe'). rye whiskey and sweet vermouth match the draft components. Aromatic bitters is hidden, which is correct: meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false}.

Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 'ORANGE PEEL · ROCKS' matches rv 7095fd3d. The ingredients match the draft components Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Demerara Syrup (role 'House prep / sweetener', which supports the word 'house') and Aromatic Bitters.

House Daiquiri: 'LIME COIN · COUPE' matches rv 14d45e57. White rum, house demerara syrup and fresh lime match the draft components; 'house' is backed by the component note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup by weight'. Sweetener before citrus follows Rob's binding role order.

Beer, cider and wine sensory lines are trims of the menu_items.menu_description rows (Czech Pilsner, Dry-Hopped IPA, Amber Lager, Dry Cider, Malbec, Pinot Grigio, Brut Rosé). Nothing was added beyond the source.

Headings Clásicos/Classics, De la casa/House Originals, De barril/Draft, Sidra/Cider, Por copa/By the Glass, Espumosos/Sparkling, De agave/Agave and Brandy map to the draft sub names. The Spanish is correct and correctly accented (Cócteles, Clásicos). The side rail '& Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa' is a venue fact from the brief, not an item fact.

ABV, region, brand, producer and vintage are missing on beer, wine and spirits. This is a known gap: the designer flagged it (proposal needs_input) and Rob has been asked. I did not count it as invented or failed.
problems: Criterion 12: the wine and beer lines read as database classes, not as appetising guest language. 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' only restate the category. 'Toasty' is a lone fragment. The trim 'Hop-forward, draft' turns the source phrase 'Hop-forward draft IPA.' into an awkward comma pair and repeats the 'De barril · Draft' heading it sits under. 'Dry, sparkling' is used twice (Dry Cider and Brut Rosé), so one line stands in for two different drinks.

Criterion 14: Brut Rosé ($13) sits under 'Espumosos · Sparkling' with no pour label. 'Por copa' covers only the sub above it, so a guest cannot tell whether 13 buys a glass or a bottle. The designer flagged this as an open question, which is honest, but the printed price is still unlabelled.

Criterion 14: the Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line breaks after 'brown butter-washed bourbon ·', leaving the separator dangling at the end of the line. It is the only cocktail that wraps, and the break reads as an error.

Criterion 13: for a Mexican cantina the agave list is thin (two tequilas, no mezcal, no Mexican lager on draft). That is a content limit, not a design one, but the only Mexican voice is the bilingual headings and the agave art. 'De agave · Agave' is a redundant pair. 'Brandy' is the only H3 left monolingual, which breaks the bilingual pattern.

Criterion 11 (minor): ingredients are set in lowercase (tequila blanco, rye whiskey) while the sources use Title Case (Tequila Blanco, Rye Whiskey). It is an acceptable consistent style, but the capitalisation is not verbatim, so I held the score below 85.
top_problem: Every fact traces to a source, but the non-cocktail descriptions are category labels ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Toasty', 'Hop-forward, draft'). For a Mexican cantina the menu reads as correct but lifeless, and the cantina voice lives only in the headings.
fixes: Replace the comma trims with the full verbatim menu_description phrases where they read better ('Hop-forward draft IPA' → drop the redundant 'draft' only if the Coordinator approves an edit; 'Toasty amber lager'; 'Dry sparkling cider'; 'Dry sparkling rosé'). Rob needs to supply grape, region and producer notes so the wines get real sensory lines instead of 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' (source: phg.menu_items.menu_description, log_id 283).

Get Rob's answer on glass or bottle for Brut Rosé and print the pour label. Until then, move 'Por copa · By the Glass' to cover the whole Vino section, or add a visible open-question marker in the proof.
Designer: rebreak the Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line so no '·' ends a line (move the separator to the start of line two, or drop it at the wrap).

Make the H3 language pattern consistent: translate 'Brandy' (for example 'Brandy · Coñac' only if Cognac VSOP is the sole item, or keep a single-language pair), and replace the redundant 'De agave · Agave' with 'De agave · Tequila' so the pair carries information.

Ask Rob for Mexican-specific inventory (a Mexican lager, a mezcal) and the missing ABV, region and brand facts so the menu reads as a cantina rather than a generic bar. Never fill these in without a data row.

lens: description quality and one guest voice (plus ingredient accuracy, venue fit, desc/price layout)
top_problem: The menu does not speak to guests in one voice, and most of it reads like a database. Margarita's 'Bright and citrus-forward' is the only line that sells a drink. Czech Pilsner's 'Crisp pale lager', Malbec's 'Dry red wine' and Pinot Grigio's 'Dry white wine' are category labels in italics. Amber Lager's 'Toasty' is a one-word fragment. The IPA's 'Hop-forward, draft' spends half its words on a pour format that its 'De barril · Draft' label already gives. Dry Cider and Brut Rosé both print the same line, 'Dry, sparkling', which also repeats their own names ('Dry', 'Brut') and the 'Espumosos · Sparkling' label. The Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned and House Daiquiri have no sensory line at all. So cocktail blocks alternate between a voiced block and a bare ingredient list. Every word is sourced (phg.menu_items.menu_description, gateway log_id 280), but the trims that avoid repeating the name have left fragments. Criterion 12 sits at the taxonomy-wording fail line.
problems: C12 (taxonomy wording): the italic lines 'Crisp pale lager' (Czech Pilsner, menu_description 'Crisp pale lager.'), 'Dry red wine' (Malbec, 'Dry red wine.') and 'Dry white wine' (Pinot Grigio, 'Dry white wine.') are faithful to the source but read as category labels, not guest language. Under the 'Vino' heading the wine lines add nothing except colour.

C12 (repeats the name or label): Dry Cider and Brut Rosé both print 'Dry, sparkling' (sources 'Dry sparkling cider.' and 'Dry sparkling rosé.'). The identical copy looks templated. It repeats 'Dry' from the cider's name, which Round 21's own name-repeat trim rule should have removed, and it duplicates the Espumosos · Sparkling label on the rosé.

C12 (fragments): 'Toasty' (Amber Lager, source 'Toasty amber lager.') is a single-word orphan. 'Hop-forward, draft' (Dry-Hopped IPA, source 'Hop-forward draft IPA.') ends on a serve format, not a flavour, and the comma splice is ungrammatical.

C12/C10 (uneven voice): only 1 of the 4 cocktails has a sensory line. Manhattan (menu_description 'Rye, sweet vermouth, aromatic bitters.'), Brown Butter Old Fashioned ('Brown butter-washed bourbon, demerara, bitters.') and House Daiquiri ('White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.') have none in the source, so they print none. That is correct, but it leaves the cocktail section in two registers. The house originals, which should carry the voice, are the mutest items on the page.

C11 verified, all sourced: garnish and glass on every cocktail trace to phg.recipe_versions (Margarita f06abb74: Lime wheel/Rocks; Manhattan 9fb77eaa: Cocktail cherry/Coupe; Old Fashioned 7095fd3d: Orange peel/Rocks; Daiquiri 14d45e57: Lime coin/Coupe). Ingredients trace to the doc components (Tequila Blanco, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup, Fresh Lime Juice; Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth; Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Demerara Syrup [House prep], Aromatic Bitters; White Rum, Demerara Syrup, Fresh Lime Juice). All 14 prices match menu_items.menu_price (log_id 280), and Junmai Ginjo is retired and correctly left off. ABV, region, producer, brand, age statement and pour size are absent everywhere (the known gap, needs Rob). Criterion 11 is held down for completeness, not accuracy.

C11 minor: the Manhattan hides aromatic bitters (per meta.public_components, aromatic-bitters false) and prints only two ingredients, although its own menu_description lists bitters. This is sourced, but guests see an incomplete Manhattan (needs_input 11).

C13: the Spanish is correct and used consistently (Cócteles, Cerveza y sidra, De barril, Por copa, Espumosos, Destilados, De agave; accents intact). But the drinks do not read as a Mexican cantina. There is one agave cocktail, a Czech Pilsner leads the draft list, there is no Mexican lager, no mezcal, and a Cognac shares the spirits column with two tequilas. The item list is locked, so this is a gap for Rob, not the designer. The $14-16 cocktail tier is high for an Iowa City college-town cantina (not verified against phg_census_zcta this round).

C14: prices sit 1 em after each name in agave green, a close and unambiguous pairing. The Old Fashioned break keeps its trailing '·' and leaves no orphan. Brut Rosé has no glass/bottle label (meta.missing 'price label: glass or bottle'), and no wine or beer shows a pour size, so the guest cannot tell what $13 or $7 buys. The italic sensory lines are 11 pt and readable in the letter preview.

Taglines: the side rail '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' and the allergy footer state no item facts, so the gate passes. The Old Fashioned's dairy allergen (brown butter) is still unconfirmed, and nothing marks it on the item.
fixes: Give the Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned and House Daiquiri a sensory line in the same voice as 'Bright and citrus-forward', sourced from their recipe_versions rationale or Rob's input. Until Rob supplies copy, flag missing_sensory_copy rather than leave the cocktail section in two registers.

Write different beer, cider and wine lines using only source words, so no two items share copy and none repeats its name or section label. For example: Dry Cider 'Sparkling' ('Dry' cut because it is in the name); Brut Rosé 'Sparkling rosé' is ruled out because 'rosé' is in the name, so flag it for Rob instead of printing the same line as the cider.

Cut 'draft' from the IPA line (its 'De barril' label already says it) and print 'Hop-forward'. Pair one-word lines such as 'Toasty' with a Rob-supplied second descriptor, or accept them as a deliberate terse register used on every beer.

Ask Rob to rewrite the menu_description for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Czech Pilsner in guest language (grape character, region, producer). 'Dry red wine' is a category label, not a description, and the region and producer gap is already open.

Add the pour size and the Brut Rosé glass/bottle label once Rob supplies them. Surface the brown-butter dairy note on the Old Fashioned when it is confirmed. Round 21 folder: /home/user/phg-harmony-app/handoff/designs/test-1-iowa-city-cantina/round-21/

lens: Venue-type fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, IA, covering census context, bilingual headings, and whether the printed facts trace to their sources (gateway log_id 284)
top_problem: The Spanish is correct but it is only a translation layer over a generic American bar list. Of 14 items, one cocktail (Margarita) and two pours (Blanco and Añejo Tequila) are Mexican. There is no mezcal, no Mexican beer and no Mexican wine. The beer section leads with a Czech Pilsner, the cocktails lean on a Manhattan and a bourbon Old Fashioned, and a Cognac VSOP gets its own Brandy heading. Nothing in the copy or the emphasis tells a guest why this is a cantina. Cocktails at 14-16 are also priced above the downtown census context: ZCTA 52240 has a median household income of $52,960, median age 28.6, 29.9% of residents aged 21-34 and 11% Hispanic/Latino. Neighbouring 52245 ($78,020) and 52246 ($62,521) are only moderately higher. Verified facts: every garnish and glass matches phg.recipe_versions through menu_items.current_recipe_version_id (Margarita Lime wheel/Rocks, Manhattan Cocktail cherry/Coupe, Brown Butter Old Fashioned Orange peel/Rocks, House Daiquiri Lime coin/Coupe). Every sensory line traces to phg.menu_items.menu_description, and every price matches menu_price. The Draft, By the Glass, Sparkling, Agave and Brandy subheads trace to build/draft_doc.json. Junmai Ginjo is correctly omitted (status retired). The Spanish headings are all correct: Cócteles, Clásicos, De la casa, Cerveza y sidra, De barril, Sidra, Por copa, Espumosos, De agave, Destilados. The side rail ('& Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa') and the allergy footer state no item facts.
fixes: Venue fit (13): the item list is not ours to change, so send the Coordinator a request to confirm or add a mezcal, a Mexican lager and one more agave cocktail. Until then, move the Destilados block ahead of or level with Wine so the agave pours carry the Mexican identity instead of sitting last next to Cognac.

Bilingual system (13): 'Brandy' is the only subhead without the Spanish · English pair. RAE Spanish also spells it 'brandy', so print it as 'Brandy · Brandy' or, if Rob signs off on retitling the source subhead, as 'Coñac · Cognac', so every label follows one rule.

Description quality (12): 'Dry, sparkling' prints twice (Dry Cider, and Brut Rosé, where 'Brut' already means dry). 'Hop-forward, draft' repeats the De barril heading directly above it. 'Toasty' is one thin word. Return to the verbatim menu_description text ('Toasty amber lager', 'Hop-forward draft IPA' without the heading echo, 'Dry sparkling rosé'), or flag missing_ingredients to ask for the grape, region, style and ABV that the draft does not carry, so none are invented.

Layout (14): the Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line breaks after 'bourbon ·', leaving a trailing separator. Set a non-breaking separator, or break before the dot. Also label the pour for wine (glass) and spirits (pour size) where the draft supplies one.

Coherence and layout (10/14): the Cider column holds one item above a large empty field, and a gap sits under the House Daiquiri before Beer & Cider. Designer note: rebalance the columns, for example by putting Cider under Draft or pairing Cider with Sparkling, so the lower grid does not read as leftover space.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png (criterion 14), plus the gate tying each price to its item. Checked against gateway log_id 281: phg.menu_items joined to phg.recipe_versions for project ddc4bb5b. All 14 approved prices match (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, House Daiquiri 14, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18). Junmai Ginjo is status='retired', so leaving it out is correct. Every garnish and glass line matches its recipe_versions row: f06abb74 Lime wheel/Rocks, 9fb77eaa Cocktail cherry/Coupe, 7095fd3d Orange peel/Rocks, 14d45e57 Lime coin/Coupe. Each italic line traces to a menu_description. The 'By the Glass', 'Draft' and 'Sparkling' labels trace to the section names and text in build/draft_doc.json.
top_problem: The price is tied to its name well: it sits 1 em after the name, eye travel is at most 0.080 of the column, and no price can be misread as another item's. The spacing around the rows is the problem, because it tells the reader the wrong grouping. In layout.json, the space between the Margarita and Manhattan blocks inside Clásicos is 14 pt. The Manhattan's COCKTAIL CHERRY · COUPE line ends at about 191.6 pt, and the DE LA CASA · HOUSE label starts at 200.6 pt, only about 9 pt later. So the break between subsections is smaller than the break between two items in one subsection, and the House label looks like a caption for the Manhattan instead of the head of the Old Fashioned group. On the item rows, the prices give no pour information. Brut Rosé 13 sits under Espumosos, which is a sibling of Por copa, so the guest cannot tell whether 13 buys a glass or a bottle (needs_input 5). Beer and spirits prices have no pour size. The one-word 'Toasty' under Amber Lager is a stub line. Across the lower grid the columns end at different heights: Sidra has one row next to three draft rows, and Spirits ends about 45 pt above Wine. That leaves empty fields beside short item-and-description stacks.
fixes: Make the space before an H3 at least as big as the 14 pt space between cocktail blocks (for example 14 pt plus the H3 line, against 7 pt now), so DE LA CASA · HOUSE reads as the head of the Old Fashioned group and not as a caption under the Manhattan. This is a layout note for the designer.

Brut Rosé 13 has no pour label: add 'copa' or 'botella' beside the price once needs_input 5 answers glass or bottle, and until then do not let its position under the wine heading imply one. Add pour sizes to the Draft and Agave labels once needs_input 2 and 6 are supplied (for example 'De barril · Draft · 16 oz').

The sensory lines read as database classes, not guest language: 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', a stand-alone 'Toasty', and 'Dry, sparkling' printed twice. 'Hop-forward, draft' also repeats its own 'De barril · Draft' label. Ask the venue for sourced tasting notes (needs_input 2 and 4) rather than printing these trims. If nothing sourced arrives, drop 'draft' from the IPA line; that is backed by the same menu_description row.

Only 1 of the 4 cocktails has a sensory line (Margarita). The Old Fashioned block is also two lines of ingredients deep while the others are one. Together this gives the cocktail blocks uneven stack heights, so the 14 pt block rhythm reads as irregular. The accuracy lens cannot add copy here, so request sourced sensory lines for the Manhattan, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri.

Venue fit: the cocktail list opens with a Manhattan in a Mexican cantina, and there is no Mexican lager or mezcal (needs_input 7). For the layout itself: balance the Sidra and Spirits columns against their neighbours, or pull the lower grid up, so no price-and-description stack sits beside a large empty field.

lens: how descriptions and prices sit together on preview-phone.png
top_problem: On the phone, each price sits right next to its item name and cannot be mistaken for another item's price. The problem is the lines under the beer and wine items. They read as database categories or repeat the name or header: 'Dry red wine' (Malbec), 'Dry white wine' (Pinot Grigio), 'Crisp pale lager', the single word 'Toasty' (Amber Lager), and 'Dry, sparkling' printed twice, under Dry Cider (repeats 'Dry' from the name) and under Brut Rosé (repeats 'Brut' and the ESPUMOSOS · SPARKLING header). 'Hop-forward, draft' repeats the DE BARRIL · DRAFT label directly above it. So the bottom half of the phone menu is a price list with category tags, and the four-line cocktail blocks above it (name/price, sensory line, ingredients, garnish · glass) sit next to beer, wine and spirits rows that are one or two lines. Rosé, beer and spirit prices also carry no pour label, so a guest cannot tell what $13 or $18 buys. Sources were not re-queried this round (protocol tool budget). I relied on proposal.md's cited gateway logs: 266 (menu_description), 259 (recipe roles), 248 (garnish/glass). Nothing on the phone showed a fact without a source, and the taglines and footer ('& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA', the allergy line) state no item facts.
fixes: Drop the italic line wherever it only restates the name or header ('Dry, sparkling' under Brut Rosé and Dry Cider, 'draft' under Dry-Hopped IPA, 'Dry red/white wine'), or leave it empty and flag the item missing_ingredients. Do not print a category tag as if it were a description (phg.menu_items.menu_description is the only source).

Get and print pour and format labels once per section header, e.g. 'Por copa · By the glass (5 oz)', 'Espumosos (glass)' and 'Destilados (1.5 oz)'. Close needs_input 2, 4, 5 and 6 so the Brut Rosé $13, the spirits' $12, $16 and $18 and the draft beer prices are no longer unlabelled.
Replace the one-word 'Toasty' under Amber Lager with a sourced sensory phrase, or remove it. A single-word line on its own row reads as orphaned on the 390 px phone.

Venue fit: bring needs_input 7 to Rob (Mexican lager, mezcal, agua fresca). A cantina with two tequilas and a Cognac as its only brandy, a Manhattan and a Daiquiri, and no Mexican beer does not read as a Mexican cantina. Also note 'Blanco Tequila' (item name) against 'tequila blanco' (Margarita ingredient): two word orders for the same spirit.

Designer note (layout, not mine to edit): the phone cocktail blocks are 3-4 lines and the beer, wine and spirits rows are 1-2. Tighten the gap between these short rows, or give the prices a shared right edge inside each short section, so the lower half keeps the same rhythm as the cocktails.
